title: Lightweight snapshot rollout sequencer with deterministic cutover
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: We need a low-friction, deterministic way to prepare and promote model rollout state across environments (hosted, dedicated, private) without long-lived in-memory locks or heavy orchestration dependencies. This PR introduces a lightweight snapshot sequencing mechanism that captures the minimal rollout state needed to drive deterministic cutover and to safely rewind when SLO gates fail. Design summary: 1) compact snapshot format (protobuf-compact) that records cohort allocations, prefix cache hints, KV cache anchors, and cutover tokens; 2) idempotent preflight checks that can be executed against a dry-run replay harness to validate latency/cost smoke signals before promoting traffic; 3) deterministic cutover algorithm that promotes cohorts in a reproducible order (session-anchored) to maintain session affinity guarantees and make post-mortem replay simpler; 4) rollback anchors: snapshots include back-reference anchors so a promotion can be reverted by applying an earlier snapshot without requiring live consensus; 5) operator reconciliation: the rollout-controller CRD accepts snapshot payloads and drives the promotion state machine without mutating live routing paths until cutover completes. What changed: - Serving runtime: new sequencer plugin (serving/rollout/sequencer.go) and snapshot serializer for compact state. - Operator: rollout-controller can accept snapshot CRDs and run preflight/dry-run (operator/controllers/rollout_controller.go). - Console: new snapshot editor and diff view for dry-run results (console/ui/rollouts/snapshot-editor.tsx). - Charts: operator CRD and RBAC updates for snapshot handling (charts/redwood-operator/templates/rollout-crd.yaml). - Tests: integration dry-run and replay harness (tests/integration/snapshot_replay_test.go). Rollout plan and safety: this PR ships behind a feature flag rollout.snapshot_sequencer. Default behavior is unchanged. The sequencer supports dry-run-only runs (no traffic change) and can be toggled to perform a live deterministic cutover once smoke signals pass. Preflight checks are idempotent and safe to run repeatedly. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for serializer and sequencer state transitions - [x] operator e2e dry-run and live promotion tests - [x] console snapshot editor wired to preview API - [x] docs and runbook for disaster recovery and manual revert - [x] CI pipeline updated to include snapshot-e2e stage Security and performance notes: snapshots are encrypted at rest and in-flight (KMS). Compact format reduces operator memory pressure; sequencer runs are bounded and yield to normal request processing. Backwards compatibility: operator tolerates old rollout CRDs; if snapshot payloads are present but feature flag is disabled, they are stored but not executed. Migration: no data migration required. Related work and context: builds on ENG-4521 (stable-session-affinity) and ENG-4680 (rollback-anchors). This is intended to reduce toil during canary/A-B promotions and to make replayable rollouts first-class. Notes for reviewers: look at sequencer preflight idempotency and the operator reconciliation loop where snapshot state is converted into a promote plan. The description above contains the runbook for toggling the feature flag and emergency revert steps.

review_comments: Marco Liu: Can we guarantee the sequencer run won't starve request threads under heavy load? Suggest yielding every 200ms and adding metrics for run_duration.
Aisha Patel: Added yielding logic + metrics (run_duration_ms, bytes_serialized). Also moved expensive validation off the hotpath into a background verifier.
Kenji Yamamoto: Operator reconciliation looks good but please add an exponential backoff on failed dry-run attempts to avoid tight retry loops.
Aisha Patel: Backoff added and tests updated to assert backoff behavior.
Sofia Becker: Verified the console diff UI and ran the e2e dry-run; approving pending changelog entry.
release_notes: Introduce a feature-flagged snapshot rollout sequencer: compact rollout snapshots, deterministic cutover, idempotent preflight dry-run, and console snapshot preview. Disabled by default; enable via rollout.snapshot_sequencer. See docs/runbooks/snapshot-rollouts.md for operator runbook and emergency revert steps.
notes_for_release: Feature flagged; recommend limited rollout to internal customers first and monitoring of sequencer.run_duration_ms, rollout.preflight_failures, and snapshot.serialize_bytes.
